material_delta: Fresh clay-direct-dev telemetry at 2026-08-26T16:51:46Z still shows active Clay legacy forge, distillery, evaluator, fabric updater and 6000 supervisor processes under owner HARD_OFF. This is host-local Clay process evidence for non-quiescence, not proof of provider calls.

Supervisor 9.04 is control-plane inconsistent: SUPERVISOR_INBOX declares 9.04 while FREE_PROVIDER_ADMISSION remains 9.03, and the 9.04 steering artifact omits active_program/product/integrated_cognition_compute_architecture fields required by tools/free_provider_admission.py. Canonical provider resolution therefore fails closed instead of resolving one coherent current HARD_OFF snapshot.

Static adversarial review found a soundness gap in tools/free_swarm_restart_authority_attribution_v2.py: SYSTEMD/CRON evidence is considered bound when it contains any legacy pattern, not necessarily the concrete matched_patterns of the root being assessed. Restart authority for one Clay process can therefore be transplanted to another root. The pinned v2 execution request is quarantined from kill authority pending a root-specific patch and adversarial tests.
Official systemd documentation reinforces that process ownership should be tied through the process cgroup/unit relation; unit configuration text alone is not the strongest PID-to-owner proof.

Trigger-2 real tokenizer execution against pinned Goekdeniz-Guelmez/Josiefied-Qwen3.5-0.8B-gabliterated-v1@591852bd verified the advertised 24-layer/1024-hidden architecture but found all digit atoms split into two tokens under leading-space rendering. Tokenizer/render ABI remains P1 and zero training/dataset credit is added.
